items.question: How do DeepWalk and LINE differ in the kind of network structure they use to learn node representations: what does DeepWalk treat as the equivalent of sentences, and what additional proximity does LINE explicitly optimize beyond observed links?
items.gold_answer: DeepWalk learns from truncated random walks by treating walks as sentences, while LINE optimizes both first-order proximity from observed links and second-order proximity based on shared neighborhood structure.
items.evidence_quote: DeepW alk uses local information obtained from truncated random walks to learn latent representations by treating walks as the equivalent of sentences.
items.evidence_quote_b: As a complement, we explore the second-order proximity between the vertices, which is not determined through the observed tie strength but through the shared neighborhood structures of the vertices.

items.question: Under what data-sparsity conditions does DeepWalk report an advantage, and how does that compare with LINE’s stated ability to scale to large graphs?
items.gold_answer: DeepWalk reports that its representations can give up to 10% higher F1 scores when labeled data is sparse, whereas LINE is described as able to scale to very large networks with millions of nodes.
items.evidence_quote: DeepW alk’s representations can provide F1 scores up to 10% higher than competing methods when labeled data is sparse.
items.evidence_quote_b: We anticipate that a new model with a carefully designed objective function that preserves properties of the graph and an efficient optimization technique should effectively find the embedding of millions of nodes.

items.question: What optimization target distinguishes LINE from DeepWalk’s learning procedure when preserving graph information, and how does DeepWalk describe its approach to learning latent representations?
items.gold_answer: LINE uses an objective that preserves local and global network structures, whereas DeepWalk learns latent representations from local information in random walks and generalizes language-model-style learning from sequences of words to graphs.
items.evidence_quote: DeepW alk generalizes recent advancements in language modeling and unsupervised feature learning (or deep learning ) from sequences of words to graphs.
items.evidence_quote_b: The model optimizes an objective which preserves both the local and global network structures.

items.question: Compare the types of network properties emphasized by DeepWalk and LINE: which method is presented as exploiting missing information well, and which method explicitly models both observed ties and shared-neighborhood similarity?
items.gold_answer: DeepWalk is presented as outperforming baselines especially when information is missing, while LINE explicitly models observed ties through first-order proximity and shared-neighborhood similarity through second-order proximity.
items.evidence_quote: Our results show that DeepW alkoutperforms challenging baselines which are allowed a global view of the network, especially in the presence of missing information.
items.evidence_quote_b: Such an intuition can be found in the theories of sociology and linguistics.
